bullets.title: NVDA: Leadership turmoil, export controls, and financing pullback ahead of earnings
bullets.body: NVDA fell ~13% w/w as CEO Jensen Huang's resignation triggered simultaneous succession, export-policy, and financing shocks. Treasury Secretary Bessent demands an external CEO hire citing 'seemingly illicit' chip sales through SE Asian data centers; prediction markets show Rene Haas (ARM) at 20% vs. Huang return at 17%. Interim CEO Kress reportedly cutting startup/infrastructure financing, and NVDA is stepping back as AI ecosystem's lender of last resort. NVDA reports earnings Tuesday with 8% implied move; key questions are SE Asian neocloud revenue exposure and guidance given new BIS export licensing rules for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil (exempt: 62% of revenue from US-HQ customers).

bullets.title: BIS new rule tightens remote access to AI chips; NVDA most exposed, BTDR down 15%
bullets.body: The Commerce Dept issued an interim final rule requiring export licenses for advanced AI semiconductor sales to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil, and restricting remote cloud access to US supercomputing for entities linked to restricted countries (D:5/Macau). NVDA's prior Singapore revenue ($10B+ quarterly, mostly US hyperscalers) is largely exempt via US-HQ customer carve-out, but SE Asian neocloud exposure remains at risk. BTDR fell 13-15% on the news given its 153MW Malaysia pipeline tied to Asian tech demand.

bullets.title: SemiAnalysis cuts AI accelerator forecasts 28-41%; semis at 11x 2028E vs 16x S&P 500
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis cut 2028-2030 AI accelerator forecasts by 28-41%, reducing cumulative 2027-2030 spending by ~$1.6T, driven by price deflation and financing constraints rather than demand collapse. AI spending grows 60% in 2027 before slowing to 21% in 2028 and 5% in 2029; accelerator spend cut 40% by 2030 while silicon area falls only 15%. NVDA bears the brunt while Broadcom and Amazon internal ASIC programs remain relatively insulated. Semis now trade at 11x 2028E earnings vs 16x for S&P 500 despite 31% consensus EPS growth; hedge fund net leverage at 5th percentile.

bullets.title: JPM Asia conference: bearish semi sentiment; ANET constructive, AMD controversial, TSM 'funding long'
bullets.body: JPM's Asia conference Day 1 showed bearish tone across semis even among longs. NVDA concerns center on leadership transition, insider selling risk, margin pressure from frontier LLMs, and regulatory capture fears; Softbank's $3.73B charge to unwind Ohio turbine orders cited as a major ROI warning signal. ANET viewed constructively as a long; CRDO/CLS sentiment mixed on Colossus customer exit risk; AMD faces controversy on server weakness and enterprise demand persistence; Korea memory seen as very cheap with 1Q HBM price hikes expected; TSM viewed as a 'funding long' by Asia pods.

bullets.title: APP: US eCommerce store count hits record weekly growth of 4.2% in Week 46
bullets.body: Citi notes AppLovin's US eCommerce store count reached 7,311, up 4.2% w/w — the largest US weekly increase to date. US store growth accelerated to a 3.2% weekly average in 4Q26 QTD vs. 1.5% in 3Q26, with global clients at 22,061 (+5.0% w/w). A 4Q26 average weekly store growth rate of 5.8% implies ~23K average store count for the quarter.

bullets.title: AMZN/DLR/EQIX: BXDC acquires $5B AWS data center stake; data center REIT activity elevated
bullets.body: Blackstone Digital (BXDC) closed its inaugural acquisition: a 75.1% stake in a 647MW, 13-building portfolio from Amazon in a sale-leaseback for ~$3.7B at a 7.0% cap rate (top of 5.75-7.0% target range), WALT 12 years (32 years fully extended), and +2.75% escalators. Pricing at ~$7.7M/MW (~50% below the $15M/MW target) reflects strategic entry. DLR plans $10B deployment in Japan over the next decade and received approval for a 156MW Illinois facility. EQIX is filing for a ~$500M DA13 data center in Dallas.

bullets.title: AMD: Completes $8.2B World Labs acquisition; TensorWave-OpenAI 457MW AMD deal
bullets.body: AMD completed its $8.2B all-stock acquisition of World Labs (spatial-intelligence AI), with Fei-Fei Li joining as EVP and Chief Scientist reporting to Lisa Su. Separately, TensorWave announced a six-year agreement with OpenAI to provide 457MW of AMD Instinct MI455X GPU capacity, expected online H1 2027 and fully deployed by early 2028 — a meaningful win for AMD's AI infrastructure positioning.

bullets.title: NET: Cybersecurity spending to rise to 2.5% of AI budgets by 2028; agent proliferation a tailwind
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley sees cybersecurity spending rising from ~1.5% to ~2.5% of enterprise AI budgets by 2028, driving ~23% cyber market CAGR, as AI lowers the expertise barrier for sophisticated attacks. More local agent deployment increases endpoint security importance, and existing Cloudflare and CrowdStrike deployments enable process and credential monitoring — positioning NET as a beneficiary of the AI security buildout.

bullets.title: MSFT: Anthropic's new collaboration tools (Whiteboards, Sheets, Meetings) pose competitive threat
bullets.body: Anthropic launched Claude Whiteboards, Sheets, Dashboards, and Meetings — directly targeting Microsoft's franchise productivity businesses. Anthropic also released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 with 30% faster output and 20% price reduction. Morgan Stanley's AlphaWise notes 64% of CIOs prefer to procure AI rather than build, with Microsoft as the leading GenAI beneficiary, though LLM providers are gaining share.

bullets.title: DKNG: NFL Week 10 flags possible low hold risk; Indiana GGR data solid
bullets.body: UBS flags possible low hold week for DKNG after 10/13 favorites won in Week 10 with all 5 biggest spread favorites winning (77% favorite win rate); 5/5 biggest-spread wins implies lower hold, posing risk to guidance. UBS recently downgraded DKNG to Neutral. Indiana October sports betting GGR came in strong at +46% y/y with hold rates expanding; DKNG's Indiana GGR +30% y/y with 10.7% hold rate (+290bps), flat 35% market share.

bullets.title: TTD/VRT: Buyback and dividend increases signal shareholder return momentum
bullets.body: Trade Desk approved an additional $731M share repurchase, bringing the total authorization to $1B. Vertiv raised its quarterly dividend 60% to $0.10/share from $0.0625. Both actions reflect balance sheet confidence amid broader market volatility.

bullets.title: TLN: Oppenheimer initiates at Outperform, $400 PT; 750MW PJM deal drives ~30% FCF/share CAGR
bullets.body: Oppenheimer initiates Talen Energy at Outperform with a $400 PT. TLN signed a 750MW seven-year PJM capacity agreement generating ~$100M/year, and base adjusted FCF/share guidance of ~$38/$48/$46-50 for 2027/2028/2029 implies ~30% CAGR from 2026-2029E. A $1.5B ASR plus additional $1.5B buyback through 2028 supports shareholder returns; AWS PPA provides contracted growth runway.

bullets.title: EXPE/ABNB: Hedgeye flags EXPE losing US share; upgrades ABNB as Best Idea Long
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes EXPE lost notable ground in US/North American room nights with ABNB more than doubling its growth rates, gaining share through hotel expansion. EXPE faces downside risk in B2C room night growth in its core US market while BKNG pushes across hotel and alternative accommodations. Hedgeye upgraded ABNB to Best Idea Long.

bullets.title: RBLX: 4Q CCUs tracking slightly below guidance midpoint per Citi
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on Roblox; Week 46 average peak CCUs were 14.7M, down 15% y/y and 3% sequentially. Early 4Q26 data implies ~$1.94B in bookings, slightly below the company guidance midpoint of $1.89B-$2.0B and below Visible Alpha consensus of $1.97B.

bullets.title: HOOD: October net deposits $15.1B beat; crypto weakness and Democratic oversight are near-term risks
bullets.body: Robinhood's October net deposits of $15.1B beat ~$13B expectations, with $6.5B from Trump Accounts implying $8.6B in core deposits. Event contracts averaged +7% ADV vs. 3Q. JPM flags crypto weakness plus incoming Democratic oversight as a risk-appetite test for HOOD and COIN near-term.

bullets.title: META: Italy fines $887M; US time spent +10% y/y; Muse #1 iOS app
bullets.body: Italy's regulator fined Meta $887M for accessing Android users' photos and videos without consent. On the positive side, Citi notes META IG US time spent +10% y/y, and Muse is the #1 iOS app download, reflecting strong engagement momentum into 4Q.

bullets.title: INTC: Shareholder lawsuit over concealed PC market slowdown
bullets.body: Intel was sued by shareholders for allegedly concealing a global PC market slowdown that resulted in a 29% stock plunge on October 30th. No new rating actions or PT changes disclosed in the item.

bullets.title: CRWV/CORZ/WULF/HUT/NBIS: Roth survey assessing enterprise AI hosting demand and provider preferences
bullets.body: Roth QSG is launching a survey of 100-150 US enterprise AI/ML procurement decision-makers to assess which GPU/HPC hosting providers they would actually contract with, including former bitcoin miners (WULF, CORZ, NBIS) vs. newer entrants like CoreWeave. Key selection criteria: price, GPU generation, power, uptime, and provider solvency. BTDR and HUT both down 11-15% today on export control and NVDA financing concerns.

bullets.title: BABA/FSLR/IREN/RGTI: Multiple universe names at 52-week lows with steep YTD declines
bullets.body: BABA is down 42.3% YTD, FSLR down 35.6%, IREN down 66.3%, and RGTI down 63.3% — all at 52-week lows as of November 16. Electronic Technology and Tech Services sectors are leading the 52-week low count (154 total lows vs. 50 highs).

bullets.title: GOOGL: Search share hits 91.0% globally, +110bps w/w; US share +30bps m/m to 85.5%
bullets.body: Citi data shows Google's global search share rose 110bps w/w to 91.0% and US search share increased 30bps m/m to 85.5%, suggesting continued dominance despite AI search competition heading into year-end.
